description: Cross-language conformance for the esm 1.0.0 classification API (esm-spec §6.3.1). The format declares two variable types, `unknown` and `parameter`; everything a solver needs beyond that is DERIVED. Five bindings deriving it independently is five chances to disagree, so these fixtures pin one answer. Each golden lists, per model node, the three unknown sets (which partition the unknowns), the four parameter sets (which partition the parameters), and the derived system_kind. Every list is sorted lexicographically by UTF-8 code point so the comparison is order-independent across languages.

functions: ode_states(model)          - unknowns appearing under D(.,t) on some equation LHS
observed_unknowns(model)   - unknowns defined by a bare-variable LHS (y ~ f(...))
algebraic_unknowns(model)  - unknowns constrained only implicitly (H*H*SO4 ~ Ksp)
is_ode_state(model, name)  - membership test for ode_states
sampled_parameters(model)  - a distribution and no update
constant_parameters(model) - neither a distribution nor an update

system_kind(model)         - derived, FIRST match wins, in this order: sde (any brownian parameter) | pde (any equation contains a spatial derivative: a D whose wrt is present and is not 't', or a grad/div/laplacian sugar op) | nonlinear (no time-derivative equation at all) | ode
partitions: ode_states + observed_unknowns + algebraic_unknowns == the model's unknowns, disjointly
brownian + discrete + sampled + constant == the model's parameters, disjointly
contract.naming: Each binding spells these in its own idiom: snake_case in Julia, Python, Rust and Go; camelCase (odeStates, isOdeState, ...) in TypeScript.
contract.model_keys: A golden's model keys are dot-paths from the document root, so a subsystem is 'Parent.Child'. Names inside each list are LOCAL to that model and are NOT namespaced.
contract.declared_system_kind: The model's explicit `system_kind` field, or null when absent. A binding MUST report system_kind from the DERIVATION, and MUST raise `system_kind_mismatch` when a non-null declared_system_kind disagrees with it.
contract.system_kind_order: The ORDER is normative, and two orderings that look equivalent are not. `pde` is tested BEFORE `nonlinear`, so a steady-state PDE (laplacian(phi) ~ f, no time derivative) is `pde` rather than `nonlinear`. `sde` is tested BEFORE `pde`, so a model carrying both a wiener parameter and a spatial derivative is `sde` -- not because it is not spatial, but because there is no SPDESystem constructor to select. Detection is a property of the EQUATIONS and never of the `domain` block: v0.8.0 removed Domain.spatial, so `domain` carries nothing spatial.

fixtures.pins: All three unknown categories and a Brownian parameter in one model — the esm-spec §6.3.1 worked example. A binding that treats every bare-variable LHS as observed without distinguishing an EXPRESSION LHS misclassifies SO4.

All six update kinds and all three distributions. Discriminates the two easy mistakes: treating any parameter with a distribution as Brownian (p_sampled and p_uniform_sampled are NOT), and treating any parameter with an update as Brownian (only p_wiener is). Also pins that the handler and `from` value forms classify the same as `expression`.
Observed unknowns declared and equated OUT of dependency order. Classification is a property of the equation set, not of traversal order.

system_kind derived from equations and parameter updates alone. Sde has no `system_kind` field and must still derive 'sde' from one wiener parameter; Nonlinear must derive 'nonlinear' from the absence of any time-derivative equation; Declared carries an agreeing field, pinning that a present field does not override the derivation.
Classification is per MODEL NODE. A binding that flattens the document first and classifies once returns a single merged answer here instead of two scoped ones.

The `pde` branch, which system_kind_variants.esm does not reach at all -- before this fixture, one of the four system_kind values was unpinned across all five bindings. Four models share ONE document-level `domain`, so a binding deriving `pde` from the presence of a domain block gets three of the four wrong. `Transient` uses a spatial `D`; `SugarOps` uses `laplacian` instead, catching a binding that recognizes only the `D` spelling; `SteadyState` has no time derivative and catches a binding testing `nonlinear` before `pde`; `StochasticSpatial` carries both a wiener parameter and a spatial derivative and must come out `sde`.
